title: 2015 AMC 8 Problem 17
statement: Jeremy’s father drives him to school in rush hour traffic in \(20\) minutes. One day there is no traffic, so his father can drive him \(18\) miles per hour faster and gets him to school in \(12\) minutes. How far in miles is it to school?

solutions.text:
Let the rush-hour speed be \(s\) miles per hour. The \(20\)-minute rush-hour trip takes \(\dfrac13\) hour, so the distance is \(\dfrac{s}{3}.\)

Without traffic, the speed is \(s+18\) miles per hour and the trip takes \(12\) minutes, or \(\dfrac15\) hour. The same distance is \(\dfrac{s+18}{5}.\)

Set the distances equal: \[\dfrac{s}{3}=\dfrac{s+18}{5}.\] Then \(5s=3s+54,\) so \(s=27.\) The distance is \(\dfrac{27}{3}=9\) miles.

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Convert \(20\) minutes and \(12\) minutes to hours.
Set the two distance expressions equal.
